title: The Rotavirus Vaccine Story: From Discovery to the Eventual Control of Rotavirus Disease.
ehr_evidence: This manuscript is a narrative review article summarizing the history, development, and global impact of rotavirus vaccines; it does not analyze primary electronic health record or linked health data.
summary: This narrative review summarizes the historical development, clinical trial efficacy, and post-licensure global impact of rotavirus vaccines, highlighting reduced mortality and hospitalizations but persistent challenges with vaccine effectiveness in low-income settings.
key_findings: Rotavirus vaccine introduction reduced rotavirus hospitalizations by a median of 59%, acute gastroenteritis hospitalizations by 36%, and diarrhea mortality by 36% in countries with routine immunization programs.
Vaccine effectiveness showed a gradient by setting: median 87% in countries with lowest under-5 mortality, 75% in intermediate, and 60% in highest under-5 mortality countries.
Rotavac demonstrated an efficacy of 56% (95% CI, 37%–70%) against severe rotavirus gastroenteritis in the first 2 years of life in India.
Rotasiil demonstrated an efficacy of 36% (95% CI, 12%–49%) in India and 67% (95% CI, 50%–78%) in Niger against severe rotavirus gastroenteritis.

Post-licensure monitoring in high- and middle-income countries observed an increased risk of intussusception of 1 to 6 excess cases per 100,000 vaccinated infants in the 1–7 days after the first dose, whereas no increased risk was seen in high-mortality countries in sub-Saharan Africa or India.
population: Children <5 years globally, with specific focus on low-, middle-, and high-income countries
limitations: This is a narrative review summarizing existing literature and clinical trial data rather than a primary observational study; it does not generate new primary data from EHR or linked health records.
